Consonantal i

Theme

Travel & transport

on the way phrase

while going somewhere

also on one’s way, on the way to, be on the way to, heading for

classical

Ter. Eun. 4.2.1: dum rūs eō, coepī egomet mēcum inter viās (Lewis & Short s.v. inter)
Cic. Att. 4.3.5: sī sē inter viam obtulerit (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 111, 404

inter viās (inter viam)

inter with the accusative

on the way, on one’s way

(vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; Cic. in epistulīs)

Literally “among the roads”: Latin puts the traveller between the roads.

Other words

  • iter habēre (+ accusative of the place, or ad) — be on one’s way to, be heading for

    also used · classical · Caes. BC 3.106.1: Caesar conjectāns eum Aegyptum iter habēre (Lewis & Short s.v. conjectō); Traupman 111: iter habēre ad (+ accusative); Traupman 404

    Caesar has the bare accusative of a country, Aegyptum; ad goes with a town or person.

See also road, by the way.
